title: Choose the new look for Truss
question: The roll picked Campus Line. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Campus Line
options.lineage: City metro maps: Delhi and Bengaluru Metro line diagrams, Vignelli-style transit graphics
options.thesis: Every internship is a station on a line that starts with you.
options.viewport: A giant line runs across the page: You, then 1st-degree, then 2nd-degree stops, each ending at a real-looking internship post. The search bar is the ticket counter.
options.risk: Turns into a metro gimmick if the lines decorate instead of showing how far each lead is from you.

raised.raise: Before you search, the query shows what Truss understood (degree, time window, role) as station chips, so nothing about the filters is hidden.
No drop shadows anywhere: depth comes only from flat colour lines crossing and overlapping.
Station spacing is one fixed unit; on small screens the line re-counts its stops instead of stretching.
Every zone carries a short line code, like a station code, so sections and results are labelled the same way everywhere.

options.label: Placement Board
options.thesis: Every lead is a flyer, pinned by someone you know.
options.viewport: A wide board of pinned internship flyers, each with a pin tag naming the person who posted it and their degree.
options.risk: Familiar: corkboards are a common student-site move and can feel like clip art if the paper isn't crafted.

options.label: Fresh Step Row
options.thesis: Freshness is the beat: posts light up on a 16-step row of the last two weeks.
options.viewport: A 16-key timeline of recent days across the top; lit keys are days with matching posts, and the chase light marks today.
options.case: Makes freshness vivid, but students identify less with drum machines and it hides the who-do-I-know story.
options.risk: Reads as a music toy if the timeline doesn't map to real dates.

options.label: Starship Terminal
options.thesis: Search as typed commands on curved phosphor glass.
options.viewport: One command line that prints results in green capitals.
options.case: Students don't see themselves in a ship terminal, and it buries who posted each lead.
options.kept: Every zone gets a code label.

options.label: Hoffmann Lattice
options.viewport: A square grid of posts in black-ruled cells.
options.case: Too formal and luxurious for students.
options.kept: Fixed units that re-count, never stretch.

options.label: Algorave Floor
options.thesis: The query is live code; edits change results.
options.case: Niche, and code-first search scares non-CS students.
options.kept: Show what changes before it applies.

options.label: Layered Papercut
options.thesis: Depth from layered flat colour, no shading.
options.viewport: A symmetrical roundel built in layers.
options.case: Beautiful but unrelated to students or job hunting.
options.kept: Depth only by flat overlap, never shadows.

options.label: Miura Fold Sheet
options.thesis: One pull unfolds the whole result sheet.
options.viewport: A folded packet that opens into results.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean student-career SaaS site, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline left, app screenshot right, logo strip and feature grid below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other career platform by design.
